title: Meta Releases Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, Its First Frontier AI Models
summary: Meta’s Superintelligence Lab launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, marking its entry into the frontier model tier with performance matching Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. Trained at the Prometheus data center in Ohio, the models introduce Active Memory and Active Focus architectures designed for long-running agentic tasks.

whyItMatters.text: Priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens via the Meta Model API.
Muse Wonder Full is restricted to Muse Code subscribers and powers the primary Muse agent.
Achieves top scores on MemoryBench for persistent context retrieval across days, weeks, and months.

articles.headline: Microsoft Announces Maia 300 Chiplet Architecture to Power Multi-Gigawatt Azure Deployments
articles.summary: Microsoft revealed its third-generation Maia 300 AI accelerator, built on TSMC's N2P process node using a modular chiplet design that separates compute, memory controllers, and I/O. The system is engineered specifically for long-context reasoning and multi-step agentic execution.
key_takeaways: Delivers 40 percent more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU systems.
Achieves up to 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200 in a full 96-accelerator configuration.
Scheduled for production rollout in 2027 to become the primary inference engine for Azure workloads.

articles.headline: Alibaba Qwen Introduces QwenGyre: Elastic Reinforcement Learning for Extreme-Long-Horizon Agents
articles.summary: Alibaba’s Qwen team detailed QwenGyre, an online reinforcement learning framework that dynamically shifts idle GPUs between rollout generation and model training. Tested on the Qwen 3.8 2.4T model, the system uses trajectory trees and KV-cache migrations over RDMA to accelerate training on tasks running for hours.
key_takeaways: Delivers a 1.38x to 1.85x end-to-end speedup over standard colocate reinforcement learning setups.
Migrates KV-cache blocks over RDMA during role switches with an average switch time of under 9 seconds.
Improved NL2RepoBench pass rates from 52.5% to 58.5% over 48 training steps on the 2.4T model.

tool_of_the_day.headline: SGLang: High-Performance Serving for Complex Reasoning and Agentic Workloads
tool_of_the_day.summary: SGLang is a fast serving framework for large language models and vision language models featuring RadixAttention for automatic KV-cache reuse. It allows engineering teams to execute complex multi-turn agentic workflows and structured generation with minimal latency overhead.
